title: Unsinkable Sam — the cat who survived three sinkings (or did he?)
sources: Wikipedia: Unsinkable Sam (Oscar/Oskar; before 1941 – 1955) — ship's cat who purportedly served with both the Kriegsmarine and the Royal Navy and survived the sinking of three ships in 1941: the battleship Bismarck, the destroyer HMS Cossack and the carrier HMS Ark Royal. Contemporary 1941 reports after Ark Royal's sinking (14 November 1941, one man killed) identify a black cat 'Oscar', found floating on a plank, said to be formerly the pet of Bismarck's crew; there is no firm evidence linking him to Bismarck or Cossack; pictures exist of two different cats identified as Oscar; Ludovic Kennedy's account of the Bismarck sinking does not mention him. The popular version: Bismarck sank on 27 May 1941 (only 115 of over 2,100 crew survived); Oscar was found on a board by HMS Cossack, whose crew named him from the signal flag 'O' for 'man overboard'; Cossack was torpedoed by U-563 on 24 October 1941 (159 killed) and sank; Ark Royal was torpedoed by U-81 and sank 30 miles from Gibraltar; Sam was found clinging to a plank, 'angry but quite unharmed'. He spent the rest of the war in a sailors' home in Belfast and died in 1955.

Photos (public domain, Wikimedia Commons / Imperial War Museum / Royal Navy): portrait of Oscar, 'cat from the German ship Bismarck'; Bismarck in Grimstadfjord, under fire and sinking, and her survivors, May 1941; HMS Rodney firing; HMS Cossack (F03); the sinking of HMS Ark Royal, November 1941
Archive film (public domain / CC0): 'Battle in Atlantic between British Navy and Bismarck' (1941); Universal Newsreel — a torpedoed tanker, 1942 — illustrative
Music: Rule, Britannia! — United States Army Strings, public domain

post.facebook:
In 1941, three warships sank in six months. One sailor survived all three. He was a cat.

At least, that's what the Royal Navy said. They called him Unsinkable Sam. The story begins on the German battleship Bismarck: in May 1941 the Royal Navy hunted her down and sank her — of more than 2,000 men, only 115 survived. Hours later, HMS Cossack found a black-and-white cat floating on a plank and named him Oscar, after the signal flag for "man overboard".

Five months later a U-boat torpedoed Cossack; 159 men died and the ship sank. The cat lived. So they moved him to the carrier Ark Royal — the ship that had helped sink Bismarck. Three weeks later Ark Royal was torpedoed too. Rescuers found him clinging to a plank, "angry but quite unharmed". He retired to a sailors' home in Belfast and lived until 1955.

But here's the catch: a cat named Oscar really was rescued from Ark Royal — the Bismarck part nobody can prove, and there are photos of two different cats both called Oscar.

Luckiest cat in history, or the best sea story the Navy ever told? 👇

youtube.description:
In 1941, three warships sank in six months — and one sailor survived all three. He was a cat.

Unsinkable Sam (Oscar) was said to have survived the German battleship Bismarck, then HMS Cossack, then HMS Ark Royal, where he was found clinging to a plank, "angry but quite unharmed". A cat named Oscar really was rescued from Ark Royal in November 1941 — but his Bismarck and Cossack days have never been proven.
